disclaimer: Reminder reference only — NOT legal authority. Season dates, areas, quotas, and limits are set annually and can change. Always verify current regulations with the Wyoming Game and Fish Department before hunting or trapping.

license_summary.predatory_animals: Coyote, jackrabbit, porcupine, raccoon, red fox, skunk, and gray wolf located outside the Wolf Trophy Game Management Area (and Seasonal WTGMA) are statutory predatory animals and may be taken without a license. All snares used for furbearing or predatory animals must have a break-away device releasing at 295 pounds or less, with loop size no greater than 12 inches.
license_summary.protected_animals: Black-footed ferret, fisher, lynx, pika, and wolverine are 'protected animals' under the 2026 guide: any trapped protected animal must be released unharmed; if injured or killed, the trapper must notify a Department law enforcement officer as soon as reasonably possible.
license_summary.trapping_license: A Wyoming furbearing animal trapping license is required to trap furbearing animals (not predatory animals). Consult WGFD for license types, fees, and trap-check periods.

species.common_name: Gray wolf (outside Wolf Trophy Game Management Area)
species.iac_reference: 2026 Wyoming Furbearing Animal Hunting and Trapping Regulations (predatory-animal definition, W.S. section 23-1-101(a)(xii))
species.notes: Outside the WTGMA and Seasonal WTGMA, gray wolves are statutory predatory animals and may be taken without a license year-round. The guide regulates snares 'for furbearing or predatory animals,' confirming trapping/snaring is a lawful method for predatory animals. All snares must have a 295-lb-or-less break-away device and 12-inch-or-less loop. Chapter 47 requires reporting of predatory-wolf kills — verify the current reporting window and method with WGFD, as the 2026 Chapter 47 final was not yet confirmed at verification.

verification.confirmation_notes: 2026 Wyoming Furbearing Animal Hunting and Trapping Regulations guide verified 2026-09-18. All furbearer season dates, the Area 1 definition, marten Area 2 (Snowy Range) dates, all beaver limited-quota areas with quotas, all beaver closed areas, the 'protected animal' definition, the predatory-animal definition (including gray wolf outside the WTGMA), the snare break-away rule, and the trapped-protected-animal release/report rules read directly from the guide. Wolf: the 2026 Chapter 47 draft (05.12.2026.2, presented July 14–15, 2026) restricts trophy-game wolves to firearms/archery during open hunting seasons; the adopted final was NOT yet confirmed, so no 2026–27 wolf hunting dates are modeled.
known_gaps: Scientific names are standard taxonomy, NOT stated in the WGFD guide — all flagged scientific_name_verified=false; 'Weasel' and 'Skunk' are null because the guide/statute are generic.
Gray wolf inside the WTGMA: no trapping season exists (firearms/archery only under Chapter 47); the 2026 Chapter 47 adopted final was not confirmed — its hunting dates are not modeled here.

Gray wolf outside the WTGMA is a predatory animal (may be taken without a license); the Chapter 47 predatory-wolf reporting requirement was not confirmed from the adopted 2026 final — verify the current reporting window with WGFD.
Section 4(b) closed areas (referenced in the Area 1 description) were not fully enumerated — users must check the guide for Section 4(b) closures.
Detailed lawful-method rules (trap-check periods, trap registration numbers) are not modeled — only the major snare rule and protection warnings are included.
River otter, swift fox, gray fox, spotted skunk, ringtail, and least weasel have no open season in the 2026 guide; they are modeled closed on that basis.
